requests.question: Using our published OXTR/IL-6 and DOCK2/PTSD chapters, give two brief evidence summaries, one for each topic. Contrast laboratory findings with mixed human IL-6 results, and explain whether DOCK2 is validated for tracking intervention response. Cite the reviewed evidence and preserve its limits.

response.answer:
### 1. OXTR/IL-6: strong laboratory mechanisms, mixed human results

The chapter finds **strong mechanistic support in selected cell systems and substantial animal evidence**, not established human anti-inflammatory efficacy. [S1] Oxytocin reduced stimulated IL-6 secretion by 56% in cultured human macrophages and 26% in endothelial cells, while separate human-donor experiments found no cytokine suppression. These are model-specific findings, not treatment-effect estimates in people. [S2] [S3]

Human findings differ by setting:
- **Acute reduction:** intravenous oxytocin attenuated endotoxin-induced IL-6 in a randomised crossover trial involving 10 healthy men. The chapter’s appraisal was abstract-based; this does not establish sustained benefit or intranasal efficacy. [S4]
- **Opposite-direction local finding:** in an 80-couple trial, women receiving intranasal oxytocin plus positive interaction had higher wound-fluid IL-6. Local repair-related IL-6 is not interchangeable with systemic inflammatory burden. [S5]
- **Corrected null result:** an eight-week trial in 61 adults with obesity reported no inflammatory-proteome treatment effects surviving multiple-testing correction; this remains conference-abstract evidence. [S6]

**Sustained systemic IL-6 lowering and clinical anti-inflammatory efficacy remain unestablished.** Lower IL-6 is not universally better, and our intervention–OXTR–IL-6–benefit pathway remains a hypothesis. [S1]

### 2. DOCK2/PTSD: association, not validated intervention-response tracking

The reviewed evidence **does not validate DOCK2 for tracking intervention response**. It remains an exploratory biological outcome, not a surrogate for recovery. [S7]

The 2017 study associated lower blood methylation at DOCK2 cg16277944 with greater PTSD symptom severity in 96 veterans, with replication in 115 independent participants. Important limits include cross-sectional male samples, a 10% discovery false-discovery-rate threshold and limited, post-hoc expression findings. [S8] Six identical-twin pairs added gene-level evidence, not confirmed replication at the same site; the chapter also records an unsuccessful exact-site replication. [S9] [S7]

A treatment study found symptom improvement without major recurrent methylation changes in four targeted genes—but those genes did **not** include DOCK2, so it supplies no DOCK2 validation. [S10] Methylation, RNA expression and clinical improvement remain separate outcomes. Neither a beneficial direction of DOCK2 change nor the proposed intervention–OXTR–DOCK2–benefit chain is established. [S7]

Both chapters are narrative evidence maps, not systematic reviews or formal certainty assessments. Source access varies, and linked reports are not independent experiments. [S1] [S7]

sources.label: S2
sources.title: Oxytocin attenuates NADPH-dependent superoxide activity and IL-6 secretion in macrophages and vascular cells
sources.authors: Szeto A, Nation DA, Mendez AJ, Dominguez-Bendala J, Brooks LG, Schneiderman N, McCabe PM.
sources.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
sources.text: Oxytocin reduced stimulated IL-6 release by 56% in macrophages and 26% in endothelial cells in the reported experiments, alongside lower NADPH-dependent superoxide activity. The cells expressed OXTR, connecting an inflammatory readout with a plausible receptor pathway.

sources.label: S3
sources.title: Oxytocin does not attenuate the ex vivo production of inflammatory cytokines by lipopolysaccharide-activated monocytes and macrophages from healthy male and female donors
sources.authors: Ross KM, McDonald-Jones G, Miller GE.
sources.text: Oxytocin did not attenuate LPS-induced inflammatory cytokine production across the tested conditions. The investigators examined donor sex, cell preparation, doses and pre-incubation as potential explanations for differences from earlier work.

sources.label: S4
sources.title: Oxytocin alleviates the neuroendocrine and cytokine response to bacterial endotoxin in healthy men
sources.authors: Clodi M, Vila G, Geyeregger R, Riedl M, Stulnig TM, Struck J, Luger TA, Luger A.
sources.journal: American journal of physiology. Endocrinology and metabolism
sources.text: Intravenous oxytocin attenuated the acute endotoxin-induced IL-6, TNF and stress-hormone response. Several regulatory mediators, including IL-1 receptor antagonist and IL-4, also decreased. Parallel human monocyte/PBMC experiments did not reproduce direct cytokine suppression.

sources.label: S5
sources.title: Effects of intranasal oxytocin and positive couple interaction on immune factors in skin wounds
sources.authors: Ditzen B, Aguilar-Raab C, Winter F, Hernández C, Schneider E, Bodenmann G, Heinrichs M, Ehlert U, Läuchli S.
sources.text: Wound-fluid cytokines depended on sex and interaction context. Among women, oxytocin combined with a positive couple interaction was associated with lower IL-1β and higher IL-6; TNF did not show the same assignment effect.

sources.label: S6
sources.title: SAT-059 Randomized Controlled Trial Examining Effects of 8 weeks of Intranasal Oxytocin on the Circulating Inflammatory Proteome in Adults with Obesity
sources.text: The inflammatory proteome analysis reported no treatment effects that survived Benjamini–Hochberg correction. Some nominal findings pointed toward increased inflammatory proteins rather than a consistent reduction.

sources.label: S8
sources.title: Genomewide DNA methylation analysis in combat veterans reveals a novel locus for PTSD
sources.authors: Mehta D., Bruenig D., Carrillo‐Roa T., Lawford B., Harvey W., Morris C. P., Smith A. K., Binder E. B., Young R. McD, Voisey J.
sources.text: Lower methylation at DOCK2 cg16277944 was associated with greater PTSD symptom severity and replicated in a separate cohort (p = 0.0028). Post-hoc blood analyses found a modest inverse methylation–expression association (r = −0.21) and a group difference in DOCK2 expression.

sources.label: S9
sources.title: Using Monozygotic Twins to Dissect Common Genes in Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Migraine
sources.text: DOCK2 was among candidate genes with methylation associations surviving gene-wise Bonferroni correction. The design matches inherited sequence and many demographic factors within twin pairs. Separate migraine analyses also implicated DOCK2.

sources.label: S10
sources.title: No evidence for intervention-associated DNA methylation changes in monocytes of patients with posttraumatic stress disorder
sources.authors: Hummel Elisabeth, Elgizouli Magdeldin, Sicorello Maurizio, Leitão Elsa, Beygo Jasmin, Schröder Christopher, Zeschnigk Michael, Müller Svenja, Herpertz Stephan, Moser Dirk, Kessler Henrik, Horsthemke Bernhard, Kumsta Robert
sources.text: Despite symptom improvement, the study found no major recurrent treatment-associated methylation changes in the tested regions of NR3C1, FKBP5, SLC6A4 or OXTR. It highlights the value of controlling blood-cell composition.
